metadata.purpose: Legal status ledger for privacy policy drafting. Distinguishes enacted law, notified rules, and commencement status.
metadata.disclaimer: This ledger is a research aid, not legal advice. Verify against primary sources before relying on it.

dpdp_act_2023.commencement_section: Section 1(2) - comes into force on dates appointed by Central Government notification

key_roles.data_principal: The individual to whom personal data relates (s 2)
key_roles.data_fiduciary: Entity that determines purpose and means of processing (s 2)

key_obligations.notice: Section 5 - itemised notice before/with consent request
key_obligations.consent: Section 6 - free, specific, informed, unconditional, unambiguous, affirmative action
key_obligations.legitimate_uses: Section 7 - closed list, no open balancing test
key_obligations.security: Section 8(5) - reasonable safeguards to prevent breach
key_obligations.breach_notification: Section 8(6) - to Board and each affected principal
key_obligations.erasure: Section 8(7) - on consent withdrawal or purpose end
key_obligations.children: Section 9 - verifiable parental consent under 18, no behavioural tracking/targeted ads
key_obligations.sdf: Section 10 - India-resident DPO, audit, DPIA, algorithmic due diligence

data_principal_rights.duties: Section 15 - no false complaints, no impersonation
data_principal_rights.gdpr_comparison: GDPR has 8 rights; DPDP has 4. No portability, restriction, objection, or automated-decision rights.

cross_border_transfer.model: Negative list - Central Government may restrict notified countries

territorial_scope.in_india: s 3(a) - processing digital personal data within India
territorial_scope.outside_india: s 3(b) - processing outside India in connection with offering goods/services to principals in India
territorial_scope.exclusions: s 3(c) - personal/domestic use; publicly available data

penalties.schedule: Maximum per instance, imposed by Board after inquiry under s 33
penalties.enforcement_status: Not enforceable as of 2026-10-01 - penalty provisions in ss 28-34 commence in tranche 3 (~May 2027)

key_rules.rule_3: Consent notice: standalone, itemised, plain language, English + 22 Eighth Schedule languages on request
key_rules.rule_6: Security safeguards: encryption, access control, logging, backup, 1-year log retention
key_rules.rule_7: Breach notification: to Board without delay + 72h detailed report + every affected principal, no risk threshold
key_rules.rule_8: Retention: purpose-end erasure, 3-year inactivity rule for large platforms, 48h pre-erasure warning, 1-year minimum retention

instruments.purpose: Establishes Data Protection Board of India

tranches.effect: Institutional machinery only. No substantive fiduciary obligations.
Opens Consent Manager registration. No new obligation on ordinary fiduciaries.

tranches.status: Not yet in force - compliance deadline
tranches.effect: All substantive obligations commence: notice, consent, security, breach, retention, children, SDF, rights, penalties.

commencement.date_discrepancy: Gazette masthead prints 13 Nov 2025; PIB backgrounder of 17 Nov 2025 states 14 Nov 2025. Rule 1 sets periods not dates. Plan to earlier date (13 Nov 2026, 13 May 2027).

current_operative_law.spdi_rules: Sensitive Personal Data or Information Rules 2011
current_operative_law.cert_in: CERT-In Directions of 28 April 2022 (6-hour incident reporting, 180-day log retention in India)
current_operative_law.note: s 43A and SPDI Rules are repealed only by s 44(2) of DPDP Act, which commences in tranche 3 (~May 2027)

data_protection_board.seating_status: Unseated as of late August 2026 - MeitY circular F. No. 2(1)/2026-Pers.I (6 May 2026) invited applications; no appointment notification located

supreme_court_challenge.case: Venkatesh Nayak v. Union of India, W.P.(C) 177/2026

acceleration_proposal.reported: January 2026 - proposal to shorten 18 months to 12

cabinet_secretary_directive.content: All ministries/states to produce time-bound DPDP compliance plans

gdpr.applicability: May apply if StableSense offers goods/services to individuals in the EU/EEA or monitors their behavior
gdpr.territorial_scope: Art 3(2) - offering goods/services to EU data subjects; monitoring behavior within EU

key_differences_vs_dpdp.legitimate_interests: GDPR: open balancing test; DPDP: closed list in s 7
key_differences_vs_dpdp.breach_threshold: GDPR: risk-based for individual notification; DPDP: no threshold, notify all
key_differences_vs_dpdp.cross_border: GDPR: adequacy/safeguards required; DPDP: permitted by default (negative list)
key_differences_vs_dpdp.penalties: GDPR: percentage of global turnover; DPDP: fixed rupee maxima
key_differences_vs_dpdp.digital_only: GDPR: covers manual filing systems; DPDP: digital only

gdpr.note: GDPR applicability must be assessed based on actual user base and offering. Do not assume all-world compliance.
